title: HR Administrator
description:
HR Administrator

Location: Ipswich (Hybrid Working Available)
Salary: £30,000 - £35,000
Hours: Monday to Friday, Full-Time

The Opportunity

We are seeking a highly organised and detail-oriented HR Administrator to join a growing HR team. This role will play a key part in delivering a seamless employee experience by providing efficient HR administration, supporting HR systems, maintaining data accuracy, and assisting with a variety of people-focused processes across the employee lifecycle.

This is an excellent opportunity for an HR professional looking to further develop their career within a fast-paced and collaborative environment.

Key Responsibilities
- Provide HR administration across the full employee lifecycle, including onboarding, employee changes and offboarding.
- Produce contracts, offer letters and other employment-related documentation.
- Coordinate onboarding activities and ensure new starters have the equipment, system access and support they need.
- Maintain accurate employee records and update HR systems in a timely manner.
- Support payroll and benefits administration, ensuring information is accurate and submitted on time.
- Respond to employee and manager queries, providing guidance on HR policies and procedures.
- Produce HR reports and assist with data analysis, audits and compliance checks.
- Ensure all HR records and processes remain compliant with company policies, GDPR and employment legislation.
- Support HR projects, process improvements and initiatives aimed at enhancing the employee experience.
- Build strong working relationships with employees, managers and key stakeholders across the business.

About You
- Previous experience in a HR support, HR coordination or HR operations environment.
- Sound knowledge of HR procedures and the employee journey from onboarding through to leaving.
- Highly organised with a strong eye for detail and accuracy.
- Able to manage a busy workload, prioritise tasks and work to deadlines.
- Strong interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to build positive working relationships.
- Confident user of Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel.
- Awareness of UK employment law and data protection requirements.
- CIPD Level 3 qualification, or currently studying towards a higher CIPD level, would be beneficial.
- Experience working with HR platforms and databases; exposure to Workday would be an advantage.

What's on Offer?
- Salary of £30,000 - £35,000
- Hybrid working available
- Monday to Friday working pattern
- Supportive and collaborative team environment
- Excellent opportunity for development and career progression within HR operations and employee experience.

If you are interested in this role, please apply with your up-to-date CV or contact Rachel Dunham at Reed Ipswich for more information.

title: Maintenance Administrator
description:
Maintenance Administrator

Ipswich, Suffolk
£14.42 an hour

Temporary assignment

Monday to Friday 8am to 5pm

A leading property maintenance and building services organisation, known for delivering high-quality work across the country, is looking for some additional help within its team. The company provides a wide range of commercial services including reactive and planned maintenance, electrical and plumbing support, and general multi-trade works.

We are seeking a confident and detail-driven Administrator to help keep daily operations running efficiently. This role sits at the heart of the maintenance team, ensuring smooth communication and supporting the coordination of ongoing works.

What you will be doing:

As a Maintenance Administrator, you will be responsible for keeping workflows organised, maintaining accurate information, and supporting the wider operational team. You'll act as a key link between engineers, clients, subcontractors, and internal departments.

Your duties will include:
- Overseeing and coordinating admin processes for both planned and reactive maintenance tasks
- Scheduling, allocating, and monitoring jobs through to completion
- Managing operatives' calendars, workloads, and appointments
- Serving as the first point of contact for clients, tenants, or residents
- Maintaining accurate systems, data, and documentation
- Providing administrative support to supervisors and managers, including reporting
- Communicating effectively with clients, internal teams, and external partners
- Identifying issues early and helping resolve them to keep service delivery on track

What We're Looking For

You'll be someone who thrives in a fast-moving environment and is able to juggle multiple tasks with confidence. Strong communication skills, great organisation, and a proactive approach are all essential.

To be successful, you must have:
- Previous administration experience within construction, maintenance, or a related sector
- Strong IT skills, particularly in Microsoft Word, Excel, and email systems
- Excellent communication and customer service abilities
- Strong organisation and time-management skills
- A positive, solution-focused mindset
- The ability to work independently while also being a supportive team player
- Flexibility to share the on-call responsibilities amongst the team

title: Project Coordinator
description:
Project Coordinator

Bury St Edmunds - 1 day per week / month

£30,000 per annum

This is an opportunity to join a growing software business providing technology to the commercial property sector, with its platform used by customers across more than 30 countries. You'll join their Delivery team, helping to coordinate customer software implementations and ensure projects remain organised and on track.

You'll support projects from initial setup through to go-live, coordinating meetings, maintaining project plans and documentation, tracking actions and milestones and keeping customers and internal teams updated. Working closely with colleagues across Product, Engineering and Account Management, you'll help make sure everyone knows what needs to happen, when it needs to happen and that actions don't get missed.

We're open to existing Project Coordinators or Project Administrators, as well as people from administration, operations, customer service or customer success backgrounds looking to move into Project Management. Previous software or project experience would be beneficial but isn't essential.

Above all, we're looking for someone who is highly organised, confident communicating with different people, comfortable managing multiple priorities and keen to build a career within projects and technology.

title: Accounts Assistant
description:
MacKenzie King are proud to be working with one of our award winning and trusted partners, based in Ipswich, close to the A14 and other major transport links. This Accounts Assistant role will sit within their long standing and supportive finance team, providing key support to the wider business as it continues to grow and succeed. The successful candidate will work closely with colleagues to ensure accurate records of customer payments are maintained and that any issues or queries are resolved promptly, helping to deliver the highest levels of customer service. Working alongside the Finance Manager, the Accounts Assistant will play a key role in ensuring service standards are met while managing a high-volume workload accurately and efficiently. This is an excellent opportunity for someone at the start of their finance and accounting career, offering the chance to develop new skills, gain valuable experience and build a strong foundation for future professional growth.

Key tasks and responsibilities
- Process daily, weekly, and monthly bank reconciliations.
- Maintain accurate and up-to-date records of all banking transactions and supporting documentation.
- Investigate, reconcile, and resolve outstanding items, discrepancies, and unmatched transactions in a timely manner.
- Process and reconcile customer payments and refunds.
- Post financial transactions to the accounting system within agreed timescales.
- Support month-end and year-end processes.
- Respond to queries in a timely and accurate manner.
- Carry out general administrative tasks to support the finance team as required.

Qualifications and experience
- Be accurate and have a high attention to detail
- Dedication to continuous improvement
- Act confidentiality and with professionalism
- Able to work collaboratively with others
- Be flexible with and supportive of others
- Educated to GCSE level (or equivalent)
- Good general numeracy and literacy skills
- Previous experience working in a similar role

To find out more about this opportunity, please contact Ben at MacKenzie King.

description: Little St Johns Surgery are looking for a Receptionist to join our busy team in Woodbridge. You will need to be flexible, highly motivated and friendly with an excellent eye for detail. The post offers 22 hours per week as follows: Monday 13:00 19:00 Tuesday 08:00 to 13:00 Thursday 13:00 to 19:00 Friday 08:00 to 13:00 *Plus occasional Saturday mornings and cover for holidays and sickness as required. Any employment offer will be subject to a full DBS check and references. Handle all telephone and general enquiries in a professional manner Make appointments for patients in accordance with practice protocols Ensure that messages and requests for visits are recorded and that the appropriate doctor or team members Ensure that any tasks requested by the clinical team are carried out Liaise with hospital and community staff Administrative duties If you would like to find out more information about this role, please see the attached job specification.

title: Administrator
description: We are seeking to recruit an enthusiastic and flexible Administrator, to join our fantastic team at Howard House Surgery in Felixstowe,with the primary focus on the role within Secretarial administration and prescriptions administration supporting with referrals and prescription requests. We are part of Suffolk Primary Care, which is a group of GP practices delivering patient care across Suffolk. The vacancy is for 3 days a week; however, this may be negotiable for the right candidate. Flexibility is crucial to accommodate training, holidays and occasional sickness. Howard House Surgery supports in excess of 8500 patients from a diverse range of backgrounds. We have an established team with a strong focus on customer service and on developing staff in order to deliver excellent standards of patient care. We use SystmOne and askmyGP to facilitate effective and efficient ways of working. You should be able to work calmly and professionally as part of a team, with the ability to multi-task. A strong command of written and spoken English with an excellent telephone manner is a must. Good time management skills and the ability to follow protocols and or instruction and attention to detail is essential. We offer a competitive salary along with other employee benefits, and the opportunity to join the NHS pension scheme. The main responsibilities of the post holder will be to ensure timely, accurate and consistent completions of referrals to secondary care, as well as accurately completing prescription requests and sending these to the appropriate pharmacy's. Working as part of a team, the post holder will be responsible for working closely with clinicians to gain the appropriate information to complete referrals and ensuring repeat medications are kept up to date and safely prescribed. They are accountable to the Administration Lead and Practice Operations Manager. Patient Administration Appointment management Results filing OOH and 111 reports filing and actions SystmOne tasks Online consultation tasks and associated actions Managing clinical correspondence, scanning & document management Shared email inboxes Care home administration Notes summarising Long term condition management Patient recalls Vaccine clinic administration Other clinic administration (LARC, minor surgery etc.) Prescription management Interpreting service bookings Medical Records Administration Patient registrations New patient checks Deduction requests Arrival of notes GP2GP transfers Sending of notes Deceased patient administration Clinical Correspondence & Reports Referrals (DXS) Medical reports, insurance requests Subject access requests Practice Administration Procurement and stock ordering Facilities and premises administration Meeting support and minute taking Rota support and locum booking administration CQC compliance and audit support Enhanced services and contractual claims and reporting

title: Senior Management Support Administrator
description: Are you an experienced administrator looking for a new and exciting opportunity? Do you have excellent communications skills and a keen eye for detail? Can you effectively manage multiple tasks and priorities? If you have said 'Yes' to each of the above then we might just have the role for you... A vacancy has arisen for a Senior Management Support Administrator supporting the West Suffolk Locality senior leadership team. The successful applicant will need to demonstrate the ability to manage a busy and varied workload, in a sometimes demanding office environment. You should be able to prioritise your work effectively, have excellent communication skills, and work as part of a team or alone using your own initiative and forward thinking. Tasks will include, but not be limited to, minutes of meetings, transcribing, supervision of staff, diary management for senior leadership team, staff training and recruitment, dealing with investigations, providing meeting support including monitoring and updating locality action logs and spreadsheets. You will need to be a focused individual, have excellent organisational ability, a good telephone manner, flexibility and a good work ethic that supports the Trust's values. It is essential you have good skills in MS Office, especially Word and Excel. Travel to meetings/other sites is also occasionally required. title: Clinical Team Administrator
description: Do you have excellent communications skills and a keen eye for detail? Can you effectively manage multiple tasks and priorities? Do you have experience of managing detailed complex information and maintaining astrong degree of confidentiality? If you have said 'Yes' to each of the above, then we might just have the role for you. This is a secondment position, working 37.5 hours per week. The post holder will be providing Administration Support to our clinicians and doctors within the team and also provide support to management. Good office based skills would be required, however, full training will be provided. We can offer a welcoming, friendly and supportive environment that puts the needs and care of our service users first and provides a responsive administration service to the West Suffolk Crisis Home Treatment Team. You will be encouraged and supported to develop your skills and knowledge. This role would see you working within a small administration team. Previous administration experience is essential. Additional training will be given for this role. You will need to be able to demonstrate the strength of your communication, prioritisation and administration skills at the same time as showcasing your knowledge of IT systems. A working knowledge of Microsoft Office Packages, including word, excel and outlook will be essential. All aspects of administration: Typing, data entry, telephone calls, booking / amending appointments, dealing with enquiries, record keeping, managing data, minute taking, Diary management. This list is not exhaustive, please refer to the job description for more detail. Please find attached our Job Description and Person Specification for more detail on your Key Accountabilities, then if you feel you have what it takes to make a difference in your local communities, click APPLY!

title: GP Receptionist
description: We are looking for a Part time member of staff to cover approx. 20 hours per week, with some weekend working. This is an exciting role that will include working within our reception. The role is very varied with every day being different. Your role is important to make sure that patients will be receiving the very best of care that they expect. Full support and training will be given. Prospective applicants are welcome to contact the Deputy Practice Manager, Abby Lake for an informal visit or further information. This position is not available to those that live overseas or require sponsorship to work in the UK. Good communication skills are essential.The role includes communicating with patients and colleagues, either face to face, via the telephone, sending texts, typing letters or emails. You will be Flexible and the ability to organise your time is important to the role. You will be working in our reception area dealing with patients within the surgery, with repeat prescription requests, the administration of medical reports or general queries. Scanning and clinically coding letters from other clinical settings, arranging to call patients for their regular chronic illness checks or managing our e-consultation system. You will be organised and work to efficient systems. You may be typing and organising the referrals to different organisations. You will be able to work within a team but also under your own initiative. To receive and book in patient's for Nurses and Doctors. To make appointments for patients. Answer telephone and deal with any resulting enquiries/requests. Accept and action all requests for repeat prescriptions whether requested in person, by e-mail, by fax or by post. To extract medical records for appointments, telephone messages, prescriptions etc. Complete the necessary documentation for temporary residents, immediate necessary treatment and emergency treatment. Charge and collect all private fees for non contracted work. Filing of various documents as required. Receive transport requests from patients and action them according to Surgery policy. Action on a daily basis any requests for home visits. Take messages for the District Nurses. Deal with incoming/outgoing post. Make tea/coffee for Doctors/Staff as required. Keep the reception area neat and tidy. Keep Doctors consulting rooms neat and tidy and clear of medical records and prescriptions that have been completed. Lock away prescriptions, make sure the surgery is as clear of filing as possible in the time allowed, ready for the morning staff. Set alarm if building is empty; lock doors and windows. Electronic summarising of patient medical records Scanning of documents into electronic patient records Typing letters either dictated by clinicians or under own discretion Dealing with emails/e-consultations by using strict protocols to signpost patient to the correct place. Adhere fully to the practice confidentiality and safeguarding policies. Undertake any other duties as may be determined from time to time commensurate with the job role.

title: Medical Receptionist
description: A rare opportunity has arisen in our Reception/Admin team to help with this busy service. We are looking for someone who can work 16-20 hours a week flexibly as needed over Monday Friday between 7.30am and 8.00pm (to 8.00pm would be only on one day a week, currently a Tuesday) when required. If you enjoy working with the public, colleagues and computer systems, then please consider applying! The job can be stressful and very busy at times, so personal resilience is required. In return you will be part of the Victoria Road Surgery Team which has a great reputation locally; is sociable and friendly with lots of charitable and fun events going on throughout the year. For further information or to arrange an informal visit before applying, please contact Assistant Practice Manager Mrs Angela Blowers at angela.blowers@nhs.net or phone 01502 572369 and ask to speak to Angela or practice manager Mrs Michelle Kears. We look forward to hearing from you. Provide a friendly welcome to patients Manage the phone system, taking calls and messages and referring patients to various services using care navigation techniques Manage the online messaging service between patients and the surgery, reading and then dealing with these patient requests and queries appropriately Explain practice appointments policies (including home visit requests) and book patients appointments with appropriate clinicians using TPP SystmOne clinical software Handing completed repeat prescriptions and other correspondence to patients having checked name, address and date of birth Be able to cover all reception positions as necessary Complete Reception tasks on SystmOne such as arranging GP requested follow-up appointments for patients JOB DESCRIPTION REPORTS TO: RECEPTION MANAGER HOURS: 16-20 hours per week Job Summary: Receive, assist and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way. Provide general assistance to the Practice team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and other visitors, in person, over the telephone and in written correspondence e.g. online messages, to patients. Job Responsibilities: To have a thorough knowledge of all Practice procedures To work in accordance with written protocols To read all correspondence sent to the Reception team or individually by task or email and respond as necessary To keep up to date with all mandatory training (most of this is online) Other tasks if needed (such as prescription and registration work), only with agreement and after the appropriate training is given Clear rooms after surgeries Ensure building security have thorough knowledge of doors/windows/alarm Make hot or cold drinks for doctors, nurse practitioners and colleagues Any other tasks allocated by managers Confidentiality: In the course of seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately. In the performance of the duties outlined in this Job Description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, Practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the Practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential. Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the Practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the Practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data. If unsure of anything in this regard the postholder must first seek advice from the Reception Manager, the Deputy Reception Manager, the Assistant Practice Manager or the Practice Manager. Do not feel pressured to give information to someone just because they demand it. Sharing confidential information when not appropriate could constitute gross misconduct and may result in disciplinary action being taken against the postholder. Health & Safety: The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the Practice Health & Safety Policy, to include: Using personal security systems within the workplace according to Practice guidelines Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way and free from hazards Reporting potential risks identified Equality and Diversity: The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognises the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with Practice procedures and policies, and current legislation Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues Behaving in a manner which is welcoming to and of the individual, is non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. Personal/Professional Development: The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the Practice as part of this employment, such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work Quality: The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the Practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs Effectively manage own time, workload and resources Communication: The post-holder should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognise peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly Contribution to the Implementation of Services: The post-holder will: Apply Practice policies, standards and guidance Discuss with other members of the team how the policies, standards and guidelines will affect own work Participate in audit where appropriate
